summary: This sermon examines Paul's farewell address to the Ephesian elders in Acts 20, where he summarizes his gospel message—repentance toward God and faith in Jesus as Lord—and explains why it offended both religious Jews and secular Gentiles. Paul warns church leaders to prioritize personal holiness and obedience over doctrinal correctness while guarding against false teachers.
key_points: Paul's core message: repentance toward God and faith in Jesus alone as Lord
Jews were offended by pride and fear of losing religious privilege; Gentiles resisted exclusive allegiance to Jesus
Church leaders must prioritize personal faithfulness and integrity before ministry tasks
Obedience and relationship with God matter more than perfect doctrine
The church was purchased with Christ's blood and requires faithful stewardship
big_idea: The gospel demands exclusive allegiance to Jesus as Lord, which offends both religious and secular culture, and the church must prioritize faithful obedience and integrity over doctrinal correctness while remaining vigilant against false teaching.
title: A SUMMER'S JOURNEY: Final Word to Ephesian Elders
